XIIII.}}</noinclude>the multitudes from sacrificing to them. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=18}}† But there came in certaine Iewes from Antioche and Icónium: and persvvading the multitudes, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Cor. 11, 25.''}}* stoning Paul, they drew him out of the citie, thinking him to be dead. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=19}}† But the disciples compassing him round about, he rising vp, entred into the citie, and the next day he vvent forth with Barnabas vnto Derbè.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=20}}† And vvhen they had euangelized to that citie, and had taught many, they returned to Lystra and Icónium, and to Antioche: {{verse|chapter=14|verse=21}}† confirming the hartes of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that by many tribulations vve must enter into the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=22}}† And when {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Vve see by this, first that SS. Paul & Barnabas were Bishops, hauing here authoritie to giue holy Orders: secondly, that there vvas euen then a difference betwixt Bishops and Priests, though the name in the primitiue Church vvas often vsed indifferently: lastly, that alvvaies fasting & praying were preparatiues to the giuing of holy Orders.}}∷ they {{sup|‖}} had ordained to them {{sup|‖}} Priests in euery Church, and had praied with fastings, they commended them to our Lord in whom they beleeued. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=23}}† And passing through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=24}}† and speaking the word of our Lord in Pergé, they went downe into Attalia: {{verse|chapter=14|verse=25}}† and from thence they sailed to Antioche, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act, 13, 2.''}}* whence they had been deliuered to the grace of God vnto the vvorke vvhich they accomplished. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=26}}† And when they were come, and had assembled the Church, they reported what great things God had done with them, & that he had opened a doore of faith to the Gentils. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=27}}† And they abode no litle time vvith the disciples.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XIIII.}}}}

''12. They vvould sacrifice.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Latria.}}This loe is the diuine worship, consisting in external sacrifice, and in acknovvledging the parties worshipped to be gods: which {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. li. 10. de Ciu. Dei c. 1''.}}may be done to no man nor creature, and therfore the Apostles refuse it vvith al possible diligence, and al the Angels and Saincts in heauen refuse that adoration by sacrifice. The Catholike Church suffereth no Priest nor other so to worship any Sainct in heauen or earth. She hath but one external Sacrifice, vvhich is in the holy Masse, of Christs body and bloud: that she offereth to God alone, and ''neither to Peter nor to Paul'' (saith S. Augustine) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. li. 8. de Ciu. c. 27''.}}''though the Priest that sacrificeth, standeth ouer their bodies, and offereth in their memories''. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Dulia.}}But other kindes of honours and dueties, inferior vvithout al comparison (how great so euer they be) to this, vve do, as the Scriptures and Nature teache vs, to al Superiors in heauen and earth, according to the degrees of grace, honour, and blessednes that God hath called them vnto, from our B. Ladie Christs ovvne mother, to the lest seruant he hath in the world. for vvhich the Heretikes vvould neuer accuse Christian people of Idolatrie, if they had either grace, learning, faith, or natural affection.

''22. Had ordained.''] The Heretikes, to make the world beleeue that al Priests ought to be chosen by the voices of the people, and that they neede no other Ordering or Consecration by Bishops, pressing the profane vse of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''χειροτονήσαντες''}}Greeke word more then the very natural signification requireth and Ecclesiastical vse beareth, translate thus, ''Ordained by election''. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Heretical translation against holy orders.}}Whereas in deede this word in Scripture signifieth, Ordering by imposition of hands, as is plaine by other wordes equiualent, ''Act. 6, 13. 1 Tim. 4. 5. 2 Tim. 1''. Vvhere the Ordering of Deacons, Priests, and others is called {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''ἐπίθεσις τῶν χειρῶν.''}}Imposition of hands: not of the people, but of the Apostles. And this to be the Ecclesiastical vse<noinclude>{{rh|||of}}</noinclude>
